title: K-flatness of the canonical open restriction of a complex
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an arbitrary open, and P an unbounded complex of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let R be the over-site restriction followed by the canonical over equivalence to O_U-modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. If P is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], then its termwise restriction R(P) is K-flat over O_U. No flatness of individual terms or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 20.26.8, specialized to the inclusion of an open; stalk criterion Tag 06YB

proof.text: Let T be Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback U.ι. Its adjunction to pushforward, from def-pc-module-pullback, makes T a left adjoint and hence additive. Uniqueness of left adjoints compares T with Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι using restrictAdjunction. Mathlib Scheme.Modules.overFunctorEquiv U then identifies the latter with the exact canonical overFunctor followed by overEquiv restriction R in the statement. Transport additivity through this natural isomorphism c:T≅R.

Apply CochainComplex.isKFlat_pullback to the underlying continuous open inclusion U.ι.base, the sheaves U.toScheme.sheaf and X.sheaf, and the structure map ⟨U.ι.c⟩. Its explicit tensorPullbackComplex is definitionally the termwise application of T to P, including the differentials; convert followed by rfl verifies the identification. Thus T(P) is K-flat.

Map c to cochain complexes with NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex and evaluate at P. For each acyclic complex F on U, map that complex isomorphism through the functor Tot(F⊗-), implemented by (curriedTensor _).map₂CochainComplex.obj F. K-flatness of T(P) supplies exactness in each degree; HomologicalComplex.ExactAt.of_iso transports it to Tot(F⊗R(P)). This is precisely the definition of K-flatness of R(P). All comparisons also hold for the empty open and unbounded complexes.

proof_origin.place: Tag 06YC specialized to the open inclusion; Tag 0096 and uniqueness of left adjoints compare the explicit tensor formula with restriction. Lean proof by K2, 2026-10-13.
